rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the People of the Book withdrew from the challenge of mutual imprecation, having been silenced by arguments and accepting humiliation and tribute, the Prophet is told to restate the conclusion gently because he longs to guide people.
rows.anchor: ولما نكصوا عن المباهلة بعد أن أورد عليهم أنواع الحجج فانقطعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation extends to Christians, Jews, and all other scriptural communities, and proposes a truth established by proofs without claiming a privilege over them.
rows.anchor: يدعو دعاء يشمل المحاجين من النصارة وغيرهم ممن له كتاب من اليهود وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet first embraces for himself what he asks of them, a teaching shared by the revealed books and the messengers.
rows.anchor: بدأ بمباشرة ما دعاهم إليه ورضى لهم ما رضي لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them People of the Book is tactful because it invokes the knowledge they possess.
rows.anchor: تلطفا بهم بما يحبون فقال : { ياأهل الكتاب } إشارة إلى ما عندهم في ذلك من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Come means rise out of the lesser and greater forms of polytheism in which they live.
rows.anchor: ارفعوا أنفسكم من حضيض الشرك الأصغر والأكبر الذي أنتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed common word is equitable and contains no unfairness or excess.
rows.anchor: ذات عدل لا شطط فيه بوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exclusive worship of God follows from His possession of all attributes of perfection.
rows.anchor: لأنه الحائز لصفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting partners also forbids believing God has a partner even when that partner is not worshipped.
rows.anchor: لا نعتقد له شريكا وإن لم نعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking one another as lords includes figures such as Ezra, Christ, rabbis, and monks who declare things lawful or forbidden.
rows.anchor: كعزير والمسيح والأحبار والرهبان الذين يحلون ويحرمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since lord can mean a teacher or nurturer, the prohibited claim is to believe a creature acts independently in what belongs uniquely to God.
rows.anchor: نبه على أن المحذور إنما هو اعتقاد الاستبداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away from Islamic monotheism, Muslims must state their disagreement; the apparently peaceful dismissal carries a severe warning of confrontation.
rows.anchor: فإن تولوا } أي عن الإسلام له في التوحيد { فقولوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording signals that turning away from this just invitation is hardly likely.
rows.anchor: بالتتعبير بأداة الشك إلى أن الإعراض عن هذا العدل لا يكاد يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims answer by following Abraham, who declared submission to the Lord of the worlds, and by fulfilling his testament to die only as Muslims.
rows.anchor: وامتثالا لوصيته إذ قال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response invokes Abraham's submission and testament, cited from 2:131 and 2:132.
rows.anchor:
{ أسلمت لرب العالمين } ) 77
[ البقرة : 131 ] وامتثالا لوصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims say they are surrendered to God's command, and the author presents the wording as an implicit warning that the Prophet may soon be ordered to fight them, as messengers customarily did.
rows.anchor: متصفون بالإسلام منقادون لأمره , فيوشك أن يأمرنا نبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslims' declaration resembles the disciples' testimony; relying on God, they would confront the opponents, who know the past victories and campaigns.
rows.anchor: بما أجاب به الحواريون المشهدون بأنهم مسلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book knew Arabs loved their forefather Abraham and that Muhammad brought Abraham's religion, as stated at 2:135.
rows.anchor: ما جبل عليه العرب من محبة أبيهم إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects this appeal to the claim that Muhammad brought the upright religion of Abraham, citing 2:135.
rows.anchor: بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of their leaders met before the Prophet; each accused the other and schemed to draw Muslims into error by claiming Abraham followed their religion, although their scriptures do not say this.
rows.anchor: اجتمع ملأ من قرابتهم بحضرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , وضلل كل منهم الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim fails chronologically: each community's religion was set by its own book and prophet, both long after Abraham; Jews trace their name to Judah, while Christians take theirs from Nazareth, Jesus's Galilean hometown.
rows.anchor: دين كل منهم إنما قرر بكتابهم , وكتابهم إنما نزل على نبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah and Gospel were revealed only after Abraham, and their defining Sabbath and Sunday practices were absent from his law; the author says they cannot deny this.
rows.anchor: وأعظم ما يتمسك به كل فرقة منهما السبت والأحد , ولم يكن ما يدعونه فيمهما في شريعة إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Abraham Muslim is coherent because Islam means yielding to proof, an old meaning present since God created reason; unlike the later Jewish and Christian labels, nobody can claim it began after Abraham.
rows.anchor: لأن الإسلام الذي هو الإذعان للدليل معنى قديم موجود من حين خلق الله العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal to reason in the rebuke means that even a fabricated scriptural claim cannot conceal the rational proof.
rows.anchor: فكيف غفلتم عن البرهان العقلي !

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They argued about Moses and Jesus, matters their scriptures mention, but did so against what they knew out of obstinacy or transgression.
rows.anchor: من أمر موسى وعيسى عليهما الصلاة والسلام لذكر كل منهما في كتابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their further dispute concerned matters absent from their scriptures and contrary to plain reason; their alleged proof does not even qualify as a doubt.
rows.anchor: وهو لا يستحق أن يسمى شبهة فضلا عن أن يكون حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their argument is in reality against God, whose knowledge encompasses everything they dispute, while they possess no knowledge except what God teaches.
rows.anchor: وأنتم تعلمون أن مجادلتكم في الحقيقة إنما هي مع الله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء والأخفش
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazari reports from Abu Amr and al-Akhfash that the hāʾ in hāʾantum is a substitute for hamza.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء وعن أبي الحسن الأخفش أنها بدل من همزة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: A report through Abu Hamdun and al-Yazidi says Abu Amr explained the form as a lengthened hamza, with hamza changed to hāʾ as Arabs do; it functions as an exclamation of wonder and rebuke.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حمدون عن اليزيدي أن أبا عمرو قال : وإنما هي { أأنتم } ممدودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was neither Jewish nor Christian, but an upright Muslim, as the preceding argument establishes.
rows.anchor: ما كان إبراهيم يهوديا } أي كما ادعى اليهود { ولا نصرانيا } كما ادعى النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people who conceal truth also lie about God and therefore about prophets, their fabrication implies that a prophet called people to worship the person falsely attributed with God's law.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لا علم لهم بقول الله سبحانه وتعالى إلا بواسطة الأنبياء عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing attributes of Jesus that exclude divinity, the passage now comprehensively denies that Jesus or any human like him called people to worship him, which by itself refutes their claim.
rows.anchor: من صفات عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام المقتضية لنفي الإلهية عنه ما لا يخفى على ذي لب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial applies to every person who shares Jesus's description, including Ezra and others, rather than addressing Jesus alone.
rows.anchor: شرع يبين أنهم كاذبون فيما يدعونه في عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ma kāna means such a thing was neither valid nor conceivable in any way.
rows.anchor: أي صح ولا تصور بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar covers any human at all, including Jesus, Ezra, and others.
rows.anchor: من البشر كائنا من كان من عيسى وعزير عليهما الصلاة والسلام وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥukm is wisdom that equips one to judge: knowledge supported by action and action perfected by knowledge; its root denotes soundly putting each thing in its proper place.
rows.anchor: الحكمة المهيئة للحكم , وهي العلم المؤيد بالعمل والعمل المتقن بالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophethood is God's report that grants the highest elevation, by which He appoints a person to call people to worship Him alone and abandon rivals.
rows.anchor: وهي الخبر من الله سبحانه وتعالى المقتضي لأتم الرفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is irrational for a human endowed with prophecy and wisdom to claim divinity: human qualities, especially changing complexion that shows contingent states, each independently rule out such a claim.
rows.anchor: لا سيما تغير بشرته الدالة على انفعالاته - مستقلة بالإبعاد عن هذه الدعوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet's call to worship himself has no support in reason or revelation and contradicts the wisdom with which he is invested, so it is certainly excluded.
rows.anchor: فلم يبق لهم مستند , لا من جهة عقل ولا من طريق نقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather, such a person tells people to be rabbānī: follow the Lord's way, combining complete knowledge with action; the added alif and nūn signal intense adherence and firmly rooted divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: تابعين طريق الرب منسوبين إليه بكمال العلم المزين بالعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rabbānī is strongly attached to God's religion and obedience.
rows.anchor: فإن الرباني هو الشديد التمسك بدين الله سبحانه وتعالى وطاعته

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said of Ibn Abbas after his death, He has died, the rabbānī of this community.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن الحنفية عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنها لما مات : مات رباني هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being knowledgeable in the Book, teaching it, and studying it lead to knowledge whose benefit is action, exhortation to good, and watchfulness toward the Creator.
rows.anchor: فإن فائدة الدرس العلم , وفائدة العلم العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form of take yourselves as lords signals that human dispositions are naturally oriented toward God without effort; angels and prophets are being rejected as lords alongside God.
rows.anchor: إيذانا بأن الفطر مجبولة على التوجه لله سبحانه وتعالى من غير كلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any worship containing even the slightest admixture is invalid; the question is framed to clear sincere worship from such impurity.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أن كل عبادة كان فيها أدنى شائبة فهي باطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage first establishes return and absence of harm, then reward, using each to imply the corresponding point left unstated before it.
rows.anchor: أثبت الانقلاب وعدم الضر أولا دليلا على حذف ضده ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A leader's death can justify desertion only if it occurs without the religion's Lord willing it; flight can help only if it changes one's survival, but neither condition applies when God determines death and lifespan.
rows.anchor: والفرار لا يكون سببا في زيادة الأجل ولا نقصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul can die except by God's will, at a fixed term that neither steadfastness advances nor flight delays.
rows.anchor: أجلا لا يتقدم عنه بثبات , ولا يتأخر عنه بفرار اصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who advance are praised and unharmed, whereas those who hold back are blameworthy and gain no benefit; courage is motivated by God's reward and retreat by preference for worldly life.
rows.anchor: فمن أقدم شكرته ولم يضره الإقدام , ومن أحجم ذممته ولم ينفعه الإحجام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking worldly recompense means acting for worldly gain, as with those who rush to seize spoils and flee ingratitude; God gives them what they sought.
rows.anchor: وهم المقبلون على الغنائم بالنهب والفارون كفرا لنعمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's ending implies that God will punish the disbelievers, but the wording omits this out of mercy toward them.
rows.anchor: وسنردي الكافرين , ولكنه طواه رفقا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking the afterlife are the grateful who stay firm in jihad and are not distracted from it.
rows.anchor: وهم الثابتون شكرا على إحسانه إليهم من غير أن يشغلهم شاغل عن الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's reward does not undermine sincerity; the higher station is work solely for God without regard to reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: ونبه على أن العمل لذات الله من غير نظر إلى ثواب ولا عقاب أعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them grateful makes the promise general by attaching the judgment to their quality of gratitude.
rows.anchor: أظهر لتعليق الحكم بالوصف وعمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding argument implies that commanded peoples divided into obedient and disobedient groups; God rewarded or punished them without being harmed or thwarted, and the story of earlier righteous people consoles the believers.
rows.anchor: فكأين من قوم أمرناهم بالجهاد , فكانوا على هذين القسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaʾayyin means how many and has many forms; among the ten canonical readings, most recite it with hamza after kāf and doubled yāʾ, while Ibn Kathīr and Abū Jaʿfar lengthen the alif and use hamza.
rows.anchor: الجمهور بفتح الهمزة بعد الكاف وتشديد الياء المكسورة , وابن كثير وأبو جعفر بألف ممدودة بعد الكاف وهمزة مكسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ibn Kathīr and Abū Jaʿfar form may be more emphatic because it compensates for a deleted letter; lengthening has stronger emotional effect and settles the heart.
rows.anchor: ولعلها أبلغ - لأنه عوض عن الحرف المحذوف - من المشهورة بالمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that his separate book treats kaʾayyin's forms, meanings, readings, pausal and connected forms, orthography, and grammatical status.
rows.anchor: استوعبته في كتابي الجامع المبين لما قيل في { كأين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning many prophets makes the consolation especially apt to Uhud, where the Prophet's companions were killed; the wording can also grammatically suggest that the prophet himself was killed.
rows.anchor: لتكون التسلية أعظم بذكر ما هو طبق ما وقع في هذه الغزوة من قتل أصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording could make prophet the subject of killed, the stronger parsing makes the many rabbānīs the ones killed; they are scholars, heirs of prophets, and followers of their way.
rows.anchor: لكن الأرجح إسناد { قتل } إلى { ربيون } أي علماؤهم ورثة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rabbānīs did not lose heart over what befell them in God's path, whether their prophet or their supporting brothers were killed by God's decree.
rows.anchor: فما تسبب عن قتل نبيهم وهنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not weaken in their work or otherwise, nor yield to enemies or ask to live under them; the author alludes to those who proposed seeking Abū Sufyān's protection through Abū ʿĀmir the monk.
rows.anchor: وما استكانوا } أي وما خضعوا لأعداهئم فطلبوا أن يكونوا تحت أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their patience earned God's love, which entails that He will grant them victory, exalt their standing, and honor them in every way.
rows.anchor: فأحبهم الله لصبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing their deeds, the passage reports their prayer: they ask forgiveness for sins and excesses, humbling themselves and attributing the setback to their own faults despite their devoted effort.
rows.anchor: فمع كونهم ربانيين مجتهدين نسبوا ما أصابهم إلى ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author urges believers to imitate them and links their repentance to the description of the God-fearing in 3:135, who remember God and seek forgiveness after wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أشار لكم سبحانه وتعالى إلى ذلك قبل الأخذ في قص القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask God to erase what caused the setback, then to strengthen their feet; the author says fear results from sin and steadiness from obedience.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الرعب من نتائج الذنب , والثبات من ثمرات الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their final request makes clear their fighting is for God rather than personal interests.
rows.anchor: قتالهم لهم إنما هو لله , لا لحظ من حظوظ النفس أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is only delusive enjoyment: Satan disguises it until people trade enduring goods for transient pleasures and regret the consequences.
rows.anchor: المتاع الذي يدلس الشيطان أمره على الناس حتى يغتروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This also consoles by recalling messengers and their communities, who persevered until death, left their possessions defenseless, and await judgment: the messengers' full victory and the disbelievers' destruction.
rows.anchor: الرسل , الذين لازموا الصبر والاجتهاد في الطاعة حتى ماتوا - وأممهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since every soul meets the same end, the obedient should strive and the disobedient restrain themselves; this rebukes the hypocrites who fled Uhud and said the martyrs would have lived had they obeyed them.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك تعريض بالمنافقين الذين رجعوا عن أحد خوف القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death cannot be escaped, and the life chosen by deserters is fleeting enjoyment that ends in regret; blessed is the one who dies pleasing the Master to whom all return and before whom they stand.
rows.anchor: فالسعيد من سعى في أن يكون موته في رضى مولاه الذي لا محيص له عن الرجوع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is consoled for denial through the trials of earlier messengers and the inevitable return, when God's allies win and His enemies suffer; the warning now includes believers facing the major trials that mark the righteous and raise them in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أعاد التسلية على وجه يشمل المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prediction is emphatic because people serving God tend to deny that their worshipped Lord will afflict them; forewarning eases the hardship by preparing them, and the passive construction distinguishes believers from hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وأفاد ذكره قبل وقوعه تهوينه بتوطين النفس عليه , وأفاد بناؤه للمفعول لتبيين المؤمن من المنافق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trials in wealth include varied spending, and trials in persons include combat and other afflictions; after Uhud, further hardship and hurtful speech from scripturalists and pagans will follow by God's established practice toward sincere servants.
rows.anchor: في أموالكم } أي بأنواع الإنفاق { وأنفسكم } أي بالإصابة في الجهاد وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing this warning after the promise of full reward encourages patience through both commanded duties and permitted calamities that lead to success.
rows.anchor: مناسبا من حيث الترغيب في كل ما يكون سببا لذلك من الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth comes before life because it can be as dear as the soul; poverty may bring humiliation, gloating, and inability to perform noble acts.
rows.anchor: وقدم المال لأنه - كما قيل - عديل الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning follows Uhud, where people were killed while pursuing wealth, and explains hostility from the People of the Book and other disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وكان ذكرها تعليلا لبغضة أهل الكتاب وغيرهم من الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people might expect ease after Uhud, God teaches that further trials and insults from all disbelievers are inevitable in this difficult world, so believers should prepare themselves.
rows.anchor: فأخبر أن البلاء لم ينقص به , بل لا بد بعده من بلايا وسماع أذى من سائر الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given scripture are Jews and Christians; the prediction also includes harm from the pagan unlettered, and the hurt may be attacks on religion arising from this battle or elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي من اليهود والنصارى { وتتقوا } أي من الأميين { أذى كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience and piety mean shielding oneself from God's displeasure, overlooking many replies while relying on answering with swords and death; these are matters worthy of firm resolve without hesitation.
rows.anchor: اعتمادا على ردهم بالسيوف وإنزال الحتوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Uhud closes by echoing 3:118, where hostility is exposed in speech, and 3:120, promising that patient piety makes enemies' schemes harmless.
rows.anchor: قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to patience and piety recalls the assurance in 3:120 that enemies' schemes will not harm the believers.
rows.anchor: وإن تصبروا تتقوا لا يضركم كيدهم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant reminder follows the prediction of abuse from the People of the Book and supports it: earlier God covenanted with prophets, and 3:183–184 says prophets fulfilled their pledges while many followers betrayed them.
rows.anchor: وأخبرهم أنه من تولى بعد ذلك فهو الفاسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed covenant warning now addresses their scholars after foretelling harm, giving believers a reason to keep the prediction of trials before them and remain steady.
rows.anchor: ثنى هنا بالتذكير بذلك العهد على وجه يشمل العلماء بعد الإخبار بسماع الأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scripture recipients broke their duty to explain the Book and concealed it, thereby harming themselves; a people who betray God's covenant will be quicker to harm believers.
rows.anchor: وإذا آذوا أنفسهم بخيانة عهد الله سبحانه وتعالى كانوا في أذاكم اشد وإليه أسرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading is to remember God's warning when it comes and endure for reward; another is to remember how predecessors squandered their covenant, lest believers repeat their deed and incur abasement and hellfire.
rows.anchor: واصبروا لتفوزوا , واذكروا إذ اخذ الله ميثاق من قبلكم فضيعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author first offered the preceding explanation, then says the necessary reading is that, after the Uhud narrative and warnings, the covenant clause attaches to an implied earlier when.
rows.anchor: هذا ما كن ظهر لي أولا , ثم بان أن الذي لا معدل عنه أنه لما انقضت قصة أحد
